relations.subject: role:query-select
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - composesWithRole. Nothing in the registry states that two roles are DESIGNED to be granted together because each is individually too narrow to be useful - requiresRole/grantsRole/impliesRole are all about a single role's own prerequisites or hierarchy, not about a documented pairing of two independently-grantable, independently-scoped roles. This is a genuinely new compositional shape: Server's finest-grained roles are explicitly built to be stacked, which has no equivalent statement anywhere in the Capella role material read so far.

notable_absence.finding: This page documents 54 individually named roles (56 section headers minus the two category headers 'Roles in Relation to Buckets' and 'User Categories'). This record deliberately extracts a selective subset - 24 roles minted or reused, plus 3 already-promoted privilege:query-* concepts reused under their role-table names - per the batch instructions not to enumerate a catalogue mechanically. Explicitly NOT individually extracted, by category: seven Query & Index roles beyond the four covered here (Manage Global Functions, Execute Global Functions, Manage Scope Functions, Query Use Sequential Scans, Execute Scope Functions, Manage/Execute Global and Scope External Functions x4, Manage/Use Sequences x2, Query Manage System Catalog); the Views category in full (Views Admin, Views Reader); Application Telemetry Writer and External Stats Reader; Eventing Manage Scope Functions; XDCR Inbound; and five of six Mobile/Sync-Gateway-adjacent roles (Sync Gateway Architect, Application, Application Read Only, Replicator, Dev Ops - only the base 'Sync Gateway' role itself is extracted, as the anchor for the naming-collision finding). None of these omissions reflects a judgment that the role is unimportant; they reflect the brief's explicit instruction to extract selectively rather than mechanically, prioritising roles that support a structural relation, roles that already exist in the registry, and roles illustrating the round's central question.

cross_component_finding: Three independent 8.0 role splits (Read-Only Admin, Local User Security Admin, External User Security Admin) all decompose the SAME distinction: separate 'can manage/view security settings' from 'can manage/view non-security cluster state', consistently routing the security-settings half into either Security Admin or Read-Only Security Admin. That consistency across three unrelated pre-8.0 roles is strong evidence this was a single deliberate 8.0 security-hardening initiative rather than three unrelated bug fixes - a fact no single role's own section states, only visible by reading all three splitInto relations together. Separately: privilege:query-update/insert/delete are minted here using the SAME plain-name convention as the three already-promoted privilege:query-select/query-manage-index/query-system-catalog, deliberately not prefixed privilege:server-*, because none of Capella's own capella-advanced-access-query-* names collide with the plain forms - the three-round-old precedent already established this is safe, and using it again keeps the whole query-privilege family internally consistent rather than half-prefixed and half-plain.
cross_product_finding: This page is the decisive evidence for the round's central question, and the answer is: Server's RBAC model does NOT fit the vocabulary built from Capella's - it is a structurally different thing that happens to reuse some of the same words, and it diverges in a more specific way than 'roles vs privileges are organized differently' (see authorization-overview.json's finding on the two-tier-vs-one-tier catalogue question). The concrete mechanism is this: Capella's role catalogue (capella-role:*, ~10 members) is FLAT and coarse - Organization Owner, Project Owner, Data Reader, Data Writer - with a separate, independently large privilege catalogue underneath supplying the fine-grained gating. Server's role catalogue (roles.md, 54 members) spans BOTH grains in one undifferentiated list: some roles are as coarse as Capella's (Full Admin, Cluster Admin) while others are as fine as an individual SQL++ statement (Query Select, Query Insert, Query Delete, Query Manage Index - each gating exactly one DML/DDL operation) - and the page's own text acknowledges this by warning that some roles are 'so limited that they're only useful when combined with other roles.' There is no Server-side equivalent of Capella's privilege catalogue as a SEPARATE enumerable thing; the closest analogue (the three already-promoted privilege:query-* concepts, now joined by three more this record) are not a distinct tier at all, they are simply Server's finest-grained ROLES, independently also called 'privileges' in N1QL reference-page prose - a genuine terminological double-use of one underlying token (query_select, query_manage_index, etc.), not two coordinated tiers. Server RBAC is compositional (many narrow roles, explicitly designed to be stacked - see composesWithRole) where Capella RBAC is combinatorial-by-catalogue (fixed roles, each pre-bundling many named privileges). And role:sync-gateway is the sharpest individual data point for the naming-collision half of the question: it is the SIXTH thing in this ontology called 'role', proving the collision problem is not confined to the Capella/Server boundary the round's brief anticipated - it recurs even within Server's own docs tree, once against a completely different product (Sync Gateway) that Server's own role catalogue has to reference by name to support a real integration.
